children.text: Dr. Mike uses the affordances of Instagram's text-based captioning features to express his deep frustration with the American healthcare system. The pictorial nature of emoji is an intentional use of social-media captioning capabilities employed by Dr. Mike to express not merely a frustration expressible in words, but one that goes beyond them—one that must be described with pure, unambiguous frustration. Dr. Mike even goes so far as to use the profane dysphemism “Shitty” to modify the noun “Healthcare system,” emphasizing his colossal frustration. For an audience quickly scrolling through the endless abyss of Instagram reels, perhaps occasionally presented with relatively mundane wellness content from Dr. Mike, the enraged visual hook of “ 😡” in this caption, paired with profanity, sourced from Dr. Mike, a brandedly optimistic, kind, and family-centric doctor, emphasizes the immense importance of the problematic American healthcare system—perhaps something worth staying for and watching.

In an attempt to engage a typical viewer of Instagram content, Dr. Mike’s clip takes advantage of an Ab Abrupto rhetorical structure to place the viewer in the middle of an illustrative anecdote. There is no introductory setup or preliminary question to set up the story; instead, while scrolling through the endless chasm of Instagram content, the rhetorical choice to place the viewer immediately into a dependent clause of a dramatic exemplum is a deliberate appeal to the core Aristotelian concept of persuasion: pathos. More specifically, the rhetorical choice to start with “Cause if someone fainted here today, we’re all calling 911” appeals to human curiosity, intrigue, and drama, as well as an innate response to danger, because of how “911” carries an important, intense connotation. The reel itself clearly stems from a longer video, but the dramatic example describing a crisis and the ethical obligations of healthcare professionals is an immediate hook that immerses the viewer in the content and aims to keep them engaged; with this bit as a clip-farmed moment from his longer videos, tailored to perform well in short-form.

Dr. Mike takes advantage of the affordances of video editing tools and, as is common on Instagram, adds overlaid captions to his videos to emphasize key ideas for his audience that are of considerable rhetorical importance relative to other points. Despite the video's predominantly bold white captions, in the middle of Dr. Mike’s story about a child with cancer, he uses the italicized yellow phrase "Make-A-Wish." This color change, juxtaposed with the consistent use of white text, invites the audience to use the captions not merely as a visual aid but as a form of rhetoric and exaggeration in their own right. Yellow, specifically, being the most visible color in the light spectrum to the human eye, triggers a neuroscience principle known as selective attention, which empirically is known to trigger a pathos—including attention and empathy—as Make-A-Wish is often associated with near-death children—the most innocent individuals enduring the most insufferable pain. The goal is to draw the viewer back into the video, given that attention span may be a constraint, given that Make-A-Wish is associated with heartbreaking events, and yellow text triggers selective attention.
